posts.title: Dermal Fillers Won't Make You Look Fake. Bad Technique Does.
posts.hook: The fear is real. The cause is not what you think.
posts.cta: Share with a friend who is nervous
posts.caption: Dermal fillers get blamed for every overdone face you have seen. The real cause is almost always placement, amount and a provider who never says stop. Here are the five things that actually make filler look fake, and how we avoid every one in Oakville.
posts.alt: Carousel about dermal fillers in Oakville: five reasons filler looks fake and how natural results are planned

ig.label: Dermal Fillers · The Honest Version
ig.coverSub: Overdone faces come from technique, not the product. Here is what to watch for.

points.b: Most overdone results are several syringes in one sitting. Natural work is often half a syringe, reviewed at two weeks, then built slowly if needed.
Filling every crease flattens a face. Supporting the cheek or the chin often softens a line better than putting filler in the line itself.
Lips, cheeks and jaw have to agree with each other. A result that ignores your natural ratios is the one people notice.

points.h: The wrong product for the area
points.b: Fillers differ in how firm and how mobile they are. Lips need softness, a jawline needs structure. One product for everything is a shortcut.

points.h: A provider who never says stop
points.b: The best result often comes from the syringe we did not open. You want an injector who is comfortable telling you that.

ig.ctaBody: Book a dermal filler consult in Oakville and we will plan the version nobody can spot.

photo.ig: woman smiling natural beauty close up

gbp.headline: *NOT* FAKE
gbp.body: Overdone filler comes from technique and amount, not the product itself.
gbp.text: Dermal fillers do not make you look fake. Too much in one sitting, chasing lines instead of shape, and ignoring proportion do. Here is how natural filler is planned at the Oakville studio. Full post on Instagram.
gbp.description:
Dermal fillers do not make you look fake. Bad technique does, and it is worth knowing what that looks like before you book anywhere.

The most common cause is amount. Several syringes in one appointment is how faces end up overdone. Natural filler work is often half a syringe, reviewed at two weeks, and built slowly only if it is needed.

The second is chasing lines. Filling every crease flattens a face, while supporting the cheek or chin often softens the line better.

The third is ignoring proportion. Lips, cheeks and jaw have to agree with each other.

Every dermal filler plan at the Oakville studio starts with a consult and an honest read of your face, including the times the right answer is less. More on Instagram.

posts.title: What Is Electrolysis? Permanent Hair Removal, Explained
posts.hook: One follicle at a time. Gone for good.
posts.caption: Electrolysis in Oakville, explained simply. A fine probe and a tiny current treat each hair follicle so it stops growing back. It works on every hair colour and every skin tone, including the grey and blonde hairs laser cannot see. Questions? Send them my way.
posts.alt: Electrolysis in Oakville explained: permanent hair removal that works on every hair colour and skin tone

ig.body: A fine probe and a tiny current treat each follicle so the hair stops growing back. Every hair colour, every skin tone, including grey and blonde.

gbp.headline: *ELECTROLYSIS*
gbp.body: Each follicle treated one at a time, so the hair stops growing back. Any colour, any skin tone.
gbp.text: Electrolysis in Oakville, explained. A fine probe and a small current treat each hair follicle so it stops growing back. It works on every hair colour and skin tone, including grey and blonde hair that laser misses. More on Instagram.
gbp.description:
Electrolysis is hair removal that treats the follicle itself, one hair at a time, so the hair stops growing back.

A very fine probe slides into the natural opening of the follicle and a small current treats the growth centre at its base. There is no cutting and no needle into the skin, and each hair takes a moment.

Because it treats the follicle directly rather than targeting pigment, electrolysis works on every hair colour and every skin tone. That includes the grey, white, blonde and red hairs that laser cannot see, and darker skin where laser needs extra care.

It takes a series of sessions, because hair grows in cycles and not every follicle is active at once. Electrolysis appointments are at the Oakville studio on Preserve Dr. Questions are answered on Instagram.

gbp.headline: *NATURAL* OR
gbp.body: The difference is ratio, shape and restraint. Not the product, and not always the amount.
gbp.text: Natural versus overdone lips, side by side. The difference is ratio and shape, not the brand of filler. Respect the border, keep the lower fuller than the upper, and stop before it is obvious. Shared with client consent on Instagram.
gbp.description:
Natural or overdone lip filler. The difference is ratio and shape, not the product.

A lip that reads as natural keeps its border, keeps the lower lip fuller than the upper, and keeps the height of the upper lip in proportion to the space above it. A lip that reads as done usually broke one of those three, most often by filling past the border or by adding volume the lip could not carry.

Amount matters less than people assume. A full syringe can look untouched and half of one can look obvious, and the variable both times is placement.

The dermal filler work worth showing is the kind nobody identifies as work. A real example from the Oakville studio, shared with client consent, is on Instagram.

ig.label: Botox Treatment · How It Works
ig.coverSub: The areas it is brilliant for, and the ones where it is the wrong tool.

points.b: It relaxes the specific muscle that folds the skin. Less folding means the line softens and, over time, stops deepening.
The two vertical lines between the brows. The most requested area, and usually the one that makes people look tired or cross when they are neither.
Treated lightly so your brows still lift. Too much here is what causes the heavy, frozen look people are afraid of.
The lines at the corners of the eyes when you smile. Softened, not erased, so your smile still reaches your eyes.
It does not add volume or lift sagging skin. Lines from lost volume need a different treatment, and I will tell you if that is you.

gbp.body: Frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet, softened while you keep your expression.
gbp.text: Botox treatment in Oakville, explained: it relaxes the muscle that folds the skin, so frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet soften while your face still moves. What it treats well and what it cannot fix, on Instagram.
gbp.description:
Botox treatment relaxes the specific muscle that folds the skin, so the line above it softens and stops deepening over time.

posts.title: Electrolysis vs Laser Hair Removal: Which One Is Permanent?
posts.hook: They are not the same treatment.
posts.caption: Electrolysis or laser? They solve different problems. Laser reduces hair over large areas and needs dark hair to work. Electrolysis treats each follicle, works on every hair colour and skin tone, and is the one recognised for permanent removal. Here is how to choose.
posts.alt: Electrolysis versus laser hair removal comparison for Oakville clients: permanence, hair colour, skin tone

ig.label: Electrolysis vs Laser · Honestly
ig.coverSub: Both remove hair. Only one is recognised as permanent. Here is how to choose.

points.b: Laser heats pigment in the hair to damage the follicle. Electrolysis treats each follicle directly with a fine probe and a small current.
Laser needs dark hair to target. Grey, white, blonde and red hairs do not absorb it. Electrolysis does not depend on colour at all.
Laser works best with contrast between skin and hair. Electrolysis suits every skin tone because it never targets pigment.
Laser is recognised as permanent reduction. Electrolysis is recognised as permanent removal, follicle by follicle.
Laser is faster for large areas like legs. Electrolysis shines on the face, brows and stubborn stray hairs laser left behind.

ig.ctaBody: Book an electrolysis consult in Oakville. We will look at your hair and skin and tell you honestly which suits you.

photo.ig: woman smooth skin portrait neutral background

gbp.headline: *ELECTROLYSIS*
gbp.body: Laser reduces hair and needs dark hair. Electrolysis treats every colour, follicle by follicle.
gbp.text: Electrolysis or laser hair removal? Laser reduces hair and needs dark hair against lighter skin. Electrolysis treats each follicle, works on every hair colour and skin tone, and is recognised for permanent removal. On Instagram.
gbp.description:
Electrolysis and laser hair removal are often treated as the same thing. They are not, and choosing the right one saves time and money.

Laser heats the pigment in the hair to damage the follicle. It is fast over large areas, but it needs dark hair to target, so grey, white, blonde and red hairs do not respond, and it works best with contrast between skin and hair.

Electrolysis treats each follicle directly with a fine probe and a small current. It does not depend on hair colour or skin tone, and it is recognised as permanent hair removal rather than reduction.

For the face, brows and the stray hairs laser left behind, electrolysis is usually the better tool. Electrolysis consults are at the Oakville studio. The full comparison is on Instagram.

posts.title: How Long Do Dermal Fillers Last?
posts.hook: Longer than you think, and it depends where.
posts.caption: How long do dermal fillers last? It depends on the area. Lips move constantly and break filler down faster. Cheeks and chin move less and hold longer. Your metabolism and the product matter too. Here is the honest range, and why top ups should be planned, not automatic.
posts.alt: How long dermal fillers last by area: lips, cheeks and chin, from an Oakville nurse practitioner

ig.label: Dermal Fillers · How Long They Last
ig.body: Lips, which move all day, usually six to twelve months. Cheeks and chin often a year or more. Your body, the product and the area decide.

gbp.headline: *HOW* LONG
gbp.body: Lips usually six to twelve months. Cheeks and chin often a year or more.
gbp.text: How long do dermal fillers last? Lips move all day and usually hold six to twelve months. Cheeks and chin often last a year or more. Your metabolism and the product matter too, so top ups should be planned, not automatic.
gbp.description:
How long do dermal fillers last? The honest answer is that it depends on where they are placed.

Lips move all day, every day, talking and eating, and that movement breaks hyaluronic acid filler down faster. Most lip filler lasts roughly six to twelve months. Cheeks and chin move far less, and filler there often lasts a year or more.

The product matters, because firmer fillers made for structure tend to last longer than soft ones made for lips. Your own metabolism matters too, and very active people sometimes notice a shorter run.

What should not happen is a top up on a timer. At the Oakville studio a top up is booked when your face needs it, not because a date came round. More on Instagram.

posts.title: Lip Filler Aftercare: Your First Week
posts.hook: Swelling is normal. Panic is optional.
posts.caption: Lip filler aftercare, day by day. Day zero is swollen, and that is fine. Here is exactly what to do and avoid in your first week so your dermal filler settles well. Save it for after your Oakville appointment.
posts.alt: Lip filler aftercare carousel: day zero result and what to do in the first week after dermal filler

ig.label: Lip Filler Aftercare · Week One

points.b: Your lips will look bigger today than they will in two weeks. Ice on and off, ten minutes at a time. Do not judge the result yet.
No gym, sauna, hot yoga or long hot showers. Heat and blood flow both make swelling worse. Sleep propped up on an extra pillow.
No pressing, pinching or massaging unless I asked you to. Hold off on dental work and, if you can, flying for a few days.
Hyaluronic acid draws water. Hydrated lips feel softer and settle more evenly. Lip balm helps too.
Small lumps early on usually settle on their own. We review at two weeks, and you can message me any time before then.

ig.ctaBody: Every lip filler client at the Oakville studio leaves with this in writing and my number.

gbp.headline: *THE* FIRST
gbp.body: Ice, water, sleep propped up. No gym, no heat, no pressing at it for 48 hours.
gbp.text: Lip filler aftercare for the first week. Ice on and off for the first day, sleep propped up, no gym, sauna or hot yoga for 48 hours, no pressing or massaging unless asked, and keep the water up. Save the post on Instagram.
gbp.description:
Your first week after lip filler, in the order it matters.

First 48 hours: ice on and off, sleep propped up on an extra pillow, and skip the gym, sauna and hot yoga because heat and blood flow both make swelling worse. Do not press, pinch or massage the lips unless you were specifically told to. No dental work, and hold off on flying if you can.

Drink more water than usual. Hyaluronic acid draws water, and dehydrated lips feel tighter and look flatter.

After 48 hours you are essentially back to normal. Small lumps in the first week are common and usually resolve on their own, but message rather than sitting and worrying. Every dermal filler client at the Oakville studio leaves with this in writing. Save it from Instagram.

posts.title: How Many Electrolysis Sessions Will I Need?
posts.hook: The honest answer is a range, not a number.
posts.caption: How many electrolysis sessions will you need? It is a course, not a single visit, because hair grows in cycles and only some follicles are active at once. Area, density, hormones and past waxing or tweezing all change the number. Tell me your area and I will give you an honest idea.
posts.alt: How many electrolysis sessions are needed, explained for Oakville clients: hair growth cycles and a course of treatment

ig.label: Electrolysis · Your Questions
ig.body: A course, not a single visit. Hair grows in cycles, so we treat follicles as they appear. Area, density and hormones decide how long.

gbp.headline: *HOW* MANY
gbp.body: A course of short sessions over several months, because hair grows in cycles.
gbp.text: How many electrolysis sessions will you need? It is a course, not one visit, because hair grows in cycles and not every follicle is active at once. Area, density and hormones change the number. Ask about your area on Instagram.
gbp.description:
How many electrolysis sessions will you need? The honest answer is a range, and it depends on you.

Hair grows in cycles, and at any moment only some of your follicles are actively growing a hair. Electrolysis treats the hairs that are visible, so the others are treated as they surface over the following weeks. That is why electrolysis is a course of sessions rather than a single visit.

The area matters, and so does how dense the hair is. Hormones matter too, and years of waxing or tweezing can make some hairs deeper and more stubborn. Sessions are usually short and get shorter as the course goes on.

At the Oakville studio you get an honest estimate for your area at your consult, not a package sold on day one. Ask on Instagram.

posts.title: Facial Balancing with Dermal Fillers: Faces, Not Lines
posts.caption: Facial balancing uses dermal fillers to bring your features into proportion with each other, instead of filling one line at a time. Often the lip you want to change looks better once the chin is supported. Here is how we think about a whole face in Oakville.
posts.alt: Facial balancing with dermal fillers in Oakville: treating proportion across chin, cheeks, lips and jaw

ig.label: Facial Balancing · Faces, Not Lines
ig.coverSub: Why the best dermal filler plan often starts somewhere you did not point to.

points.b: Facial balancing looks at how your chin, lips, cheeks and jaw relate. Small changes to one feature change how the others read.

gbp.headline: *FACES*
gbp.body: Facial balancing brings chin, cheeks, lips and jaw into proportion with each other.
gbp.text: Facial balancing with dermal fillers treats the whole face, not one line at a time. Supporting the chin or cheeks often changes how the lips and mouth read. Less product, placed in the right two or three places. On Instagram.
gbp.description:
Facial balancing uses dermal fillers to bring your features into proportion with each other, rather than filling one line at a time.

The features of a face are read together. A soft chin can make lips look too full or a nose look larger, so supporting the chin is sometimes the whole answer. A little cheek support can soften the lines around the mouth without putting filler into those lines at all.

It is rarely about lots of product. It is about the right amount in the two or three places that change how everything else reads, often staged across visits and reviewed at two weeks.

Facial balancing consults at the Oakville studio start with photographs and an honest conversation, and you leave with a plan either way. More on Instagram.
